body.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\), and \(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\).  Under the regular random-design and geometric beta-mixing conditions, the accepted anchor/extrapolation estimator obeys
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0]
 \le C R_\star.
\]
This upper bound uses no lower local-modulus condition.  If \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\), then, still over the base Holder class,
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0]
 \asymp R_\star
 \asymp
 \left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\right\}
 \vee\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{2\lambda/d}
 \vee N^{-\lambda}.
\]
Thus the nonredundant oracle/generated-proxy boundary is
\(N^{-\lambda}\asymp
 \{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\}\vee
 \{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\).  The displayed smoothing component in \(R_{\mathrm{or}}\) is algebraically dominated for fixed \(S\) and is not a fourth nonredundant phase.  On the independent-calendar subclass the spacing term is \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  In the scalar specialization \(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), and \(n_1=n\), the unreduced bookkeeping form is
\[
 n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}
 \vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda},
\]
and its second term is dominated by the maximum of the first and third.
body.justification: For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the anchor estimator attains the geometric-mixing rate over the clarified base model, and the explicit lower subexperiments all satisfy donor independence from the entire joint panel.
body.gap: The logarithmic spacing term cannot be removed under the triangular-array mixing envelope; the independent-calendar subclass has the no-log rate.
body.consumer: Applications compare treated replication, random spacing, and donor location without treating the dominated smoothing expression as a fourth phase.
body.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad
 D_T=\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{2\lambda/d}.
\tag{1}
\]
On the event that the attained anchor at \(z_0\) is coercive, the comparison
argument (15)--(16) in \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} applies; this also
covers the case in which the genuinely attained bandwidth is one.  If the
anchor at \(z_0\) is unavailable, squared error is at most \(16B^2\) because
the estimator and target both lie in \([-2B,2B]\).  The fixed-scale occupancy
part of \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} bounds the probability of
this event by \(CT^{-2}\).  Minkowski's inequality, followed by the two
moment conclusions of that lemma, therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0]
 \le C\bigg[&A+
 \left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2\\
 &+D_T+N^{-\lambda}\bigg]
 \le CR_\star.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
Here \(T^{-2}\le CD_T\), because \(0<2\lambda/d\le2\).  The use of the
clarified donor assumption inside the conditional comparison is legitimate
by the factorization (14) proved in \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier}.

The apparent smoothing component is redundant.  With
\(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and \(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\), direct exponent arithmetic and
the weighted arithmetic--geometric inequality yield
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}
 \le a_s\vee b.
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(S\) is fixed, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2
 \le2S\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
      +2T^{-2\lambda/d}
 \le C(A+D_T).
\tag{4}
\]

Assume now \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\).  Each lower bound below is
an embedded subexperiment of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  For the
treated-mean channel, use independent uniform exact designs, a common
admissible donor law independent of the entire joint panel, and constant
untreated surfaces.  Translate the two-point outcomes (9) in
\texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} into a fixed positive subinterval of
\((0,B)\).  Set treated potential wealth equal to the observed translated
outcome and untreated event wealth equal to the constant surface.  Taking
\(W_{si,-1}=1\), the horizon-zero return equal to wealth minus one, and all
later returns zero verifies \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.  All model assumptions
hold, including donor independence from the full joint panel, and the
two-law inequality (8) in \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} gives risk at
least \(cA\).

The construction in \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} gives two
base-class laws with risk at least \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  For a fixed auxiliary
error probability in \((0,1/2)\),
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} gives two base-class
laws with a common subprobability measure of positive mass and target
separation \(cD_T^{1/2}\).  Applying the same elementary two-law inequality
gives risk at least \(cD_T\).  The largest of these three bounds, together
with (4), proves
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0]
 \asymp A\vee D_T\vee N^{-\lambda}\asymp R_\star.
\tag{5}
\]

On the independent-calendar subclass, the independent part of
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} replaces \(D_T\) in (2) by
\(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  For the matching converse, place a cube of radius
\(r_T=cT^{-1/d}\) around \(z_{01}\), and choose two uniformly bounded Holder
regressions which coincide off that cube and differ at its center by
\(c_1r_T^\lambda\).  The density upper bound gives hit probability at most
\(C_Xv_dr_T^d\) for each design point.  Calendar independence and a
sufficiently small fixed \(c\) imply
\[
 \Pr\{X_{1t}\text{ misses the cube for every }t\}
 =(1-p_T)^T\ge c_2>0.
\tag{6}
\]
On this event the two observed response laws coincide, while their targets
differ by \(c_1T^{-\lambda/d}\).  Restricting their common law to this event
and applying (8) from \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} proves the lower
squared-risk term \(cT^{-2\lambda/d}\).

Finally, set \(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), and \(n_1=n\).  Formula (2)
then has the unreduced bookkeeping form
\[
 n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}
 \vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda}.
\]
Formula (4) proves that its second term is dominated by the maximum of its
first and third terms, giving the asserted three nonredundant phases and the
stated oracle/generated-proxy boundary.
